kind: assumed or cited inputs; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository
number_format: Rates and limits are written as exact fractions in strings ("3/20" is 15%); analyze.py computes with them exactly and rounds only when it writes results.json.

forecasters.note: Assumed true revision rates for beliefs held at confidence 0.85 or more. 'Calibrated' is this lesson's reading, not the repository's: every revision is treated as an error, and a forecaster who states confidence c is wrong on a share 1 - c of such statements.

rate_15_percent.description: Revised 15% of the time: the most a forecaster calibrated at confidence 0.85 would be wrong.

rate_10_percent.description: Revised 10% of the time: calibrated at confidence 0.90.

rate_5_percent.description: Revised 5% of the time: calibrated at confidence 0.95.

rate_one_third.description: Revised one time in three: the recorded share, taken as the true rate. Overconfident under the lesson's reading.

interval.normal_quantile_note: 97.5% point of the standard normal distribution, used only for the approximate interval shown for comparison.

test.note: Decision rule 'call the forecaster overconfident when c or more of n high-confidence beliefs are revised'. The error rates are choices, not observations.

accumulation.assumption: High-confidence belief files keep being recorded at the pace of the six counted at the pin: six between the earliest last_updated among them and the timestamp of the record. This only sets a scale. The six were not recorded at a steady pace, and two of them are written by the applying script from recommendations.

nudge_simulation.assumption: Each cycle sees a fresh, independent sample of sample_per_cycle high-confidence beliefs from a forecaster whose true revision rate is fixed. The recorded loop does not work that way (it re-reads the same belief files on every cycle): this is the rule's best case, not a model of the project.
nudge_simulation.report_note: The policy schedules the calibrator weekly and human oversight at least quarterly: 13 cycles is one quarter of weekly cycles, 52 is one year.

rules.total_clamped_as_in_the_applier: Pinned rule: a recommendation is produced when the observed rate exceeds the trigger; its nudge is max(-cap, -gain * rate); the stored total is the previous total plus the nudge, clamped to [-cap, +cap].
rules.per_cycle_cap_only: The same nudge, capped per cycle as the policy's guardrail is worded, with no limit on the running total. Not what the pinned script does.
rules.two_sided_comparison_rule: Hypothetical, not in the repository: nudge = clamp(-gain * (observed rate - target), -cap, +cap), with the pinned gain and cap and the pinned trigger as target. It moves up when the observed rate is below the target and down when it is above. No limit on the running total.
rules.two_sided_with_the_total_clamp: The hypothetical two-sided rule with the stored total clamped to [-cap, +cap].

hypothesis_thresholds.note: Written before the first run of analyze.py and not changed afterwards.

cited_producer.note: Cited, not observed at the pinned Demerzel commit. The script that computes the count lives in the ix repository; it was read once at the commit below, outside the fixture. Its file on the main branch had the same Git blob on 2026-10-13.

counting_rule.high_confidence: every *.belief.json file of the two belief folders, current and archived, whose confidence is at least high_confidence_line
counting_rule.revised: the high-confidence files that lie in the archived folder

cited_producer.claim_template: {revised} of {high} high-confidence beliefs (>= {line}) were later revised (overconfidence_rate={rate}). Revisions evidenced by archived prior versions: {files}. Nudge magnitude capped at +/-{cap}/cycle per ml-governance-feedback-policy.

recommendation_confidence.formula: min(cap, base + per_belief_file * number of belief files read)

planted_move.note: In a copy of the snapshot, one current high-confidence belief is treated as archived. The recount and the rebuilt claim must both change.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical incident-review log for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
